text.p: Analysis of the strengths and weaknesses of Fenerbahce and Galatasaray who meet in the Turkish first division at Fenerbahce Stadium on Sunday (1700 GMT).

Playing style: Fenerbahce try to play a Brazilian-style soccer instituted by 1994 World Cup-winning coach Carlos Alberto Parreira and continued under present trainer Sebastiao Lazaroni, Brazilian national coach in 1990.

Nigerian Uche Okechukwu and Dane Jes Hogh have formed an impressive defensive partnership. A second Nigerian, Augustine "Jay Jay" Okocha, attempts to link the midfield with Bosnian striker Elvir Bolic and his usual partner, the lanky Saffet Sancakli, up front.

Strengths: Fenerbahce have the strongest defence in the Turkish league, conceding the fewest goals this season (11 in 20 games). The ability of Bolic to find scoring positions and the flair of Okocha could provide the rather predictable Galatasaray defence with more than a few headaches.
In September Fenerbahce scored a morale-boosting 4-0 away success over their great rivals -- Galatasaray's only league defeat to date.

Weaknesses: Lazaroni is under great pressure to get results and controversial club chairman Ali Sen has even hinted at a change at the top. Okocha is often accused of being more of a showman than a team player and fans feel he has done little to take the place of Oguz Cetin in midfield who was sold last year. Rumours of dispute within the camp are rife, with some foreign team members unhappy with the unrelenting media attention.

Motivation: If Fenerbahce can win this game they will go level on points with Galatasaray at the top of the table. Fenerbahce are keen to retain their hold on the title and firmly stamp their authority over their Istanbul rivals.

Team (probable): Fevzi Layic, Ilker Yagcioglu, Uche Okechukwu (Nigeria), Jes Hogh (Denmark), Erol Bulut, Selahattin Ozbir, Mustafa Dogan, Augustine "Jay Jay" Okocha (Nigeria), Tayfun Korkut, Elvir Bolic (Bosnia), Saffet Sancakli.

Playing style: Romanian Georgi Hagi, though not Galatasaray's captain, is beyond doubt their team leader, controlling play from the midfield. He is the key player with much depending on whether he is on form or not. Either Romanian Adrian Ilie or local Arif Erdem will partner top scorer Hakan Sukur up front. Sweeper Bulent Korkmaz provides the last line of defence with three in front of him and a third Romanian, Iulian Filipescu scampering up and down the right flank.
Strengths: A unified and harmonious team under universally popular ex-national team coach Fatih Terim.
Firepower. Suker is the league's top scorer with 20 goals as the team rattled in 51 goals in 20 games to lead the league by three points.

Weaknesses: Form. Galatasaray have drawn all three of their three league matches played since the new year break , scoring only one goal. The sensitive Sukur's scoring feats have dried up in the second half of the season with the team putting in lacklustre performances against second-rate opposition.

Motivation: This is a crucial game for Galatasaray, not only to avenge their psychologically scarring 4-0 September disaster, but to justify their position at the top of the league following a poor restart after the break. In a league dominated by these two teams, together with Besiktas and Trabzonspor, the games between the two decide the eventual champions.
Team (probable): Mehmet Sen, Bulent Korkmaz, Feti Okuroglu, Vedat Inceefe, Iulian Filipescu (Romania), Suat Kaya, Tugay Kerimoglu, Georgi Hagi (Romania), Ergun Pembe, Hakan Sukur.
